column1: # Line-count-pinned grandfather ledger for the Markdown 500-line file cap
# under go/ (issue #6187), the Markdown sibling of
# scripts/lib/dirgate-grandfather.tsv: a closed list of the .md files that
# already exceeded the cap when the gate landed, so the gate lands green on
# today's tree and new or growing files fail immediately.
# This file is the single source of truth for the cap check.
# scripts/lib/markdown-line-cap-core.sh reads it directly -- there is no
# generated Go mirror the way dirgate has one, because the Go cap is enforced
# by a golangci-lint plugin that walks the Go AST and cannot see a .md file at
# all. Nothing regenerates this file; edit it by hand, using
# `bash scripts/verify-markdown-line-cap.sh --pin <path>` to measure the row.
# Columns (tab-separated): path<TAB>line_count
#   path       - repo-root-relative path of the Markdown file.
#   line_count - the file's exact line count (awk NR, which counts a final
#                unterminated line that `wc -l` would miss) at the commit
#                this row was pinned.
# The rule the pin is checked with is `live <= line_count`, NOT dirgate's
# `live == file_count`. A count match is not a pin match, and the two ledgers
# deliberately assert different things:
#   - A file whose live count EXCEEDS line_count FAILS. Pinning the number
#     rather than allowlisting the filename is the entire point: a bare
#     filename allowlist would let go/internal/storage/postgres/README.md
#     drift from 3766 lines to 5000 without a gate ever going red. Between
#     the #6187 census and this commit four of these files had already grown
#     -- reducer/AGENTS.md by 6 lines, storage/cypher/README.md by 86,
#     query/README.md by 4, query/evidence-notes.md by 38 -- which is the
#     drift this column measures.
#   - A file whose live count is BELOW line_count passes, and the gate prints
#     a non-fatal NOTE asking for a re-pin. dirgate hard-fails a shrink to
#     force its ratchet down; that is right for a ledger whose rows move when
#     FILES move, and wrong here. Markdown shrinks a line at a time on
#     ordinary prose edits, and requiring a re-pin for each one would make
#     every documentation edit under go/ re-touch this one shared file, which
#     serialises documentation edits against each other -- the exact cost
#     #6187 warned a second dirgate-shaped ledger would carry. The bounded
#     price of the softer rule: a file that shrinks to 600 lines may regrow
#     to its pin before failing. It can never exceed the pin.
# There is deliberately NO content digest column. A digest would fail on
# every edit that leaves the line count alone -- most edits -- and would add
# no protection against the growth this gate measures.
# A row is STALE, and the gate hard-fails on it, once its file no longer
# exists or has been brought to 500 lines or fewer. The change that splits a
# file deletes its row in the same commit; the list only shrinks.
# What a good split looks like, so this gate teaches rather than only blocks:
# these are three documents with three audiences, and the repo already names
# them (docs/internal/agent-guide.md, "Documentation Workflow"). doc.go is
# the godoc contract, README.md is human architecture and operational
# context, AGENTS.md is scoped agent instruction. An over-long README.md is
# usually carrying material that belongs in one of the other two, or in a
# topic-scoped sibling (see go/internal/query/read-models.md, or the
# evidence-notes.md files below). Cut along that boundary. Do not cut at
# whichever line brings the number under 500.
# Pinned at 5570de3454a942449a339168041fd87c215e7fa1 with
# `bash scripts/verify-markdown-line-cap.sh --pin <path>`.
